texts.work: Ionas, Vitae Columbani liber I (with epistula and carmina)

evidence.quote: Verba igitur Nametis usque perduxit in exemplari (x), unde libri A 1a.b.c.2 pendent, suo loco mota ... in altero autem exemplari (y) ordo rerum intactus relictus erat
talisque condicionis codex non solum is erat, qui a Fredegario librarioque B adhibitus est, sed extat adhuc A 3, quocum facit imperfectus A 4.
Praestantissimus alterius classis codex B 1a, quocum fere convenit B 1b, ab eodem patre (d) prognatus ... B 2, qui alio stemmate ad eundem avum referendus est
stemma delineare libet hoc: Archetypus / x y / α A1a A1b β / A2 A3 A4 / A1b* B1a B1b B2 [diagram, OCR garbled]

texts.notes: Stemma Archetypus -> x, y is clear; exact placement of A2 and of the Greek-letter nodes is garbled in OCR, check the printed diagram p. 48. A5 group sides now with A3 now with A4 (assigned to y because it lacks the Chagnoald passage like y); A1c switches to A2 in the second half; Fredegar is an indirect witness of y; class B is a later retractatio descending from y.

texts.work: Ionas, Vitae Columbani liber II (Athala, Eustasius, Miracula Evoriacensia, Bertulfus, Miracula Bobiensia)

evidence.quote: In libro secundo recensendo non eadem qua in priore subsidiorum copia abundavimus, deficiente exemplari y, deficientibus etiam codicum praestantiorum x partibus magnis.
Menda enim iam in ipso deprehenduntur quae familiae A 1 neque unum exemplar librarius adhibuisse videtur, sed duo diversae originis.
Quae cum ita sint, totum libri secundi fundamentum ad codices A 1 et A 2 iam relatum est.

texts.notes: For book II all extant witnesses descend from x (y lost), so the editor's top split under the archetype is not represented; recorded the two families A1/A2 as branches (classes_only). B1a used two exemplars and agrees with A1b/A1b1, so placed with A1, but it is contaminated. Each Vita in book II has a different witness set (conspectus p. 56).

evidence.quote: V. Walarici ad codices meliores 1. 2 tantum recensui, e quibus in adiaphoris priorem anteposui, cum alter textum locis nonnullis inprimis in fine leviter retractatum exhibeat. Reliquos interpolatores turpiter depravaverunt

texts.notes: Classes are implied only by the numbering 1-4; Krusch states no relation between them and did not examine classes 3-4 closely. Edition rests on 1 and 2.

evidence.quote: Codices in tres classes distinxi.
Ad textum recensendum libros 1a. 2a. 3a adhibui, e quibus 1a. 3a propius inter se coniuncti sunt, medius sermonem haud raro impolitum ope grammaticae interdum emendasse videtur.
Ad hanc autem classem plerique codices pertinent et, nisi fallor, etiam quarta cum ipsa in appendice convenit, dum in Vita magis cum 1 facere videtur.

texts.notes: Pairing 1+3 against 2 rests on one sentence about the three collated codices; the referent of 'hanc classem' (class 2 or 3) is ambiguous. Class 4 sides with 1 in the Vita but with the other class in the appendix (c. 28-29).

evidence.quote: Ex his libris 1a. b. 2 ad textum recensendum fere soli adhibendi erant, cum classis 3. leviter retractata esset ... Codices autem 1a. b inter se adeo coniuncti sunt, ut consentientes pro uno teste habendi sint.

texts.notes: Three numbered classes; no statement on how 1, 2 and 3 relate. Labbe's edition derives from a codex like 2.

sigla.manuscript: Ph. Labbe, Nova bibl. mss. II (1657), from a codex of S. Austrigisilus de Castro

evidence.quote: Textum Miraculorum genuinum solus codex 2 exhibet; classis enim 3, quae in c. 13. desinit retractationem quandam continet.

texts.notes: Class 3 is a retractatio ending at c. 13; Labbe's edition is from a codex 'paulo melioris notae' than 2 and is used to correct it. Grouping Labbe with 2 rests on Krusch's identification of the same source codex (p. 191).

evidence.quote: Codices 1. 2. 3 unam familiam faciunt, e quibus praestantia eminet 1, dum sermonem V. Amati admodum immutat 3. Libri alterius familiae 4. 5. tantam librariorum libertatem licentiamque subierunt

texts.notes: Two families, no archetype discussion; same codices serve all three Habendum vitae.

evidence.quote: Codices 1. 2. 3 unam familiam faciunt, e quibus praestantia eminet 1, dum sermonem V. Amati admodum immutat 3. Libri alterius familiae 4. 5. tantam librariorum libertatem licentiamque subierunt

texts.notes: Codex 5 contains only V. Amati; 3 has V. Romarici added by a s. XIII hand.

evidence.quote: Codices 1. 2. 3 unam familiam faciunt, e quibus praestantia eminet 1, dum sermonem V. Amati admodum immutat 3. Libri alterius familiae 4. 5. tantam librariorum libertatem licentiamque subierunt

texts.notes: Only codices 1, 2 (imperfect), 3 transmit it, all of one family; 4 omits V. Adelphii and 5 has only V. Amati, so no top division is stated for this text.

evidence.quote: Classis 3 cum altera arta necessitudine coniuncta est, sicut ex locis colligi licet his

ex exemplari pendentes, quod haud ita longe post Walahfridum propriam viam ingressum videtur esse. Inter ipsos enim et reliquos libros inprimis primae classis nulla fere aut certe perrara necessitudo intercedit
Unicus quem quartae classi attribui codex raro cum aliis libris convenit ... modo cum libris 2 facit, modo cum 3c.
Codices Walahfridianos in classes distribuendi arduum opus erat ... neque ex ipsis stemma satis certum componi licet.

texts.notes: Five classes; only 2+3 are explicitly joined. Krusch says no certain stemma can be built. Codex 6 follows class 2 at first, then class 5 (two exemplars), so it is left out of the branches; 7 derives from the exemplar of 2g* but was collated with other classes. Class 4 is sporadically contaminated.

texts.work: Vita Rusticulae sive Marciae abbatissae Arelatensis (auctore Florentio)

sigla.manuscript: Codex Andreae Chesnii (lost; known through Duchesne and Mabillon editions)

evidence.quote: Libris inter se discrepantibus lectio vera modo ex hoc modo ex illo eruenda erat.

texts.notes: Two witnesses, one only through editions; no filiation stated (implicitly independent).

evidence.quote: Codex vetustissimus 1, quocum arte coniunctus est 1*, ex exemplari persimili pendens ... Libri 3a. b ex exemplari eodem exscripti sunt

texts.notes: Groups 1/1*, 2 and 3a/b are stated; their mutual relation is not. Recensions B and C are listed but not edited.

sigla.manuscript: Londiniensis Add. 11880, fol. 150-160 (second copy in same codex)

evidence.quote: Utraque igitur recensio A et B ex exemplari deperdito (X) pendet, cuius textum primigenium modo hic, modo ille servavit.

texts.notes: A and B are two recensions printed in parallel where they diverge. A1 and A2 are two copies in one codex. B2b and B3 'fortasse vinculo quodam cohaerent'; B3 seems collated with several exemplars.

evidence.quote: Codices in duas familias discedunt, cum libris 1. 2 reliqui omnes oppositi sint. Codex 1 ... neque ipsi comparari potest qui ex eodem exemplari pendet liber 2 pessime interpolatus.

texts.notes: Siglum of the lost Compendiensis is garbled in OCR ('4//', '4Jf'); check p. 386.

evidence.quote: Inter utramque classem A et B id interest, quod A elocutionem rusticam melius servavit, B vero ... Codices A1 et A2 ex exemplari eodem pendent
unde concludi licet archetypum B codici A4 propinquius fuisse quam A 1. 3.
pendentes uterque ex exemplari quodam A ... Sunt autem hi libri aliique, quos quamvis stirpe alienos in hac classi collocavi, suo quisque modo interpolati

texts.notes: Krusch states that the B archetype is closer to A4 than to A1/A3, which undercuts A as a top branch; the A/B split here is a class division, not a stated archetype split. Class X is explicitly heterogeneous (X1a/b derive from an A exemplar).

evidence.quote: E tribus in quas libros distribui classibus prima sola (A) ex exemplari pendet neque immutato neque interpolato ... adsunt autem in altera (B), dum in tertia (C) sermonis pristini iacturam lugemus.
E tribus quas ad Vitam recensendam adhibui classibus A B C prior archetypi simillima est ... Sunt autem libri A bipartiti unusque A 1 contra reliquos A 2. 3. 4 stat.
Dum enim textus V. Fursei in D 1 ad classem C pertinet, libri Austriaci D 2 ex exemplari meliore A pendere videntur

texts.notes: Three classes with internal structure stated, but no statement on how A, B, C relate to each other. B2e and A1* mix readings of other classes; C4d1/2 interpolated from B1. D codices assigned to A/C per p. 431.

evidence.quote: Pendent igitur C2a.b ex exemplari alio atque reliqui, idque praeter lectiones splendidas etiam menda continebat pauca

texts.notes: C3, C4a-c, C5 share a Vulgate correction; C6 are a conflated Vita+Virtutes type and were not used. Check that C6 belong with the non-C2 group.

sigla.manuscript: Bollandist edition, Cat. cod. hagiogr. Paris. I (1889)

evidence.quote: Est autem illud codicibus diversae originis subiunctum. Dum enim textus V. Fursei in D 1 ad classem C pertinet, libri Austriaci D 2 ex exemplari meliore A pendere videntur

texts.notes: The stated filiation concerns the Vita text in these codices, not the Additamentum itself; split D1 vs D2 inferred from that and the numbering.

texts.work: Arbeo, Vita vel passio Haimhrammi episcopi et martyris Ratisbonensis

evidence.quote: Ut codices A2. 3. 4 ex exemplari correcto Y pendent ... ita studii illius primordia quamvis rarissima in archetypo eo iam adfuisse videntur, ex quo omnes qui supersunt libri pendent, scilicet in Z
ex ipsa praestantia exemplaris X, proavi codicum B, concludi licet, quod totam classem A aliquoties superans haud raro lectionem A 1 confirmaverit
Variae codicum affinitates primo aspectu explicantur stemmate hoc: Z / X / A1 Y B / A2 α B1 γ δ B4 / A3 β B2a B2b B2c B2d B3a B3b / A4a A4b [diagram, OCR garbled]

texts.notes: Reading the diagram as Z -> A1, Y, X(-> B); check the printed stemma p. 470, since X could sit under Z with A1/Y as separate lines or as a single A node. Y was corrected from a class-B codex (contamination). A5 (Siglum from Suyskens' S. Germain copy) and B5 placement are not shown in the OCR'd diagram.

evidence.quote: Ex locis enim Sulpicianis colligi licet tertiam potius classem in his diversitatibus praestare, ita ut proavus codicum 1. 2 verborum collocationem suo arbitratu immutasse videatur
Ad huius vero familiaritatem et 3c se applicat et 3d. Ultimus denique qui totus retractatus est codex 4 ex exemplari simili 3a manifesto pendet.

texts.notes: Two stated groups: 1.2 (common proavus) vs class 3 (+4).

evidence.quote: Cum Marciliacense coenobium pro Musciacensi c. 23. in utroque substitutum sit, inde librum archetypum eorum originem traxisse patet.
ita ut hunc ex illo pendere paene certum habeam.

texts.notes: 2 and 3 share a Marciliacum archetype which Krusch thinks was 'almost certainly' copied from 1, so there is no split below the archetype (single branch). He also allows that a reader corrected that exemplar from a better codex.

Apographon Fr. Bosqueti (lost; used by Labbe)

evidence.quote: Libri 2 ex exemplari multo deteriore eoque mutilo pendent, sed nonnullae lectiones melioris notae vel in eis deprehenduntur

evidence.quote: Haud modicum temporis intervallum inter A et B intercessisse ex his argumentis colligi licet.

texts.notes: A (older recension, single codex A1) is the edited text; B is a later retractatio cited in the apparatus. Not a single tradition: the A/B split is between redactions.

texts.work: Vita Eligii episcopi Noviomagensis libri duo (Dado/Audoinus)

evidence.quote: Duae in priore libro codicum classes ita inter se distinguendae sunt, ut libris 1, quibuscum facit 7, potior calculus, alter vero reliquis omnibus accedat ... ex exemplari hic illic depravato reliquos pendere
Libros 2 et 3 ex eodem exemplari pendere manifestum est

texts.notes: Top split 1(+7) vs rest holds for book I only; class 1 lacks book II, which rests on classes 2-9 alone. Codex 7 goes with class 1 in book I but with class 2-type elsewhere; 3* siglum from OCR '3'y'; Epistulae and the verse 'liber III' are short appended pieces (skipped).

evidence.quote: Textum ad praestantissimum codicem 1 recensui, discrepantiam lectionum alterius classis apparatui attribuens, quippe quae sermone immutato a loquendi more aevi illius haud raro recedat.
